newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - Jun Ifo business index.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Jun Ifo business index.

text.p: Following are comments from economists on the June Ifo business climate index, which showed a rating of 96.0 for west Germany compared with a revised 95.4 in May.
GERNOT NERB, ECONOMIST, SALOMON BROTHERS, FRANKFURT:

"The figures are more or less in line with expectations. It is a bit stronger. The improvement of the business situation reflects a better profit situation. That is our main conclusion. The weak mark and higher profits from exports are reflected.
"But some businesses think this will slow down and is reflected in the slight weakening of expectations.
"Our forecast is that employment will stabilise in the coming months and pick up next year.
"For the time being, there is no reason for the Bundesbank to raise rates. I think the Bundesbank will be comfortable with the mark at between 1.70 and 1.83 to 1.84, but not at higher brackets."
MATHIAS HAFFNER, ECONOMIST AT BZW IN FRANKFURT
"This not a big sensation. The east German figure shows construction in the east is still not so good. In spite of the dollar rise, the expectations in west Germany are not so good.
"The tempo we saw in the first few months is not sustainable, but there still is potential on the upside."

"We expect a further recovery in the manufacturing sector and it is a good sign for Germany. We also expect improvement in the second half of the year for employment but in fact next year there will be a bigger improvement.
"I think the German government will make every effort to meet the criteria (for the single European currency) and I think we will meet them at the end of the year.
"If there is not a crisis in the mark, then the Bundesbank will wait before raising rates."
KIT JUCKES, BOND AND CURRENCY STRATEGIST, NATWEST MARKETS, LONDON:
"It is good for the bits of the economy that are doing better. Germany's problem is the weakness of the emplyoment situation and this number doesn't tell us anything about that."
He also said on currency markets: "There is only so many times you can intervene verbally without doing anything."
